problem: Touchdown depends on raw Street View panoramas that cannot be redistributed under Street View's terms of service, so researchers must scrape them via the API. This is error-prone, non-reproducible because panoramas change over time, and cannot honor PII takedown requests.
motivation: Street View offers world-scale outdoor visual data for language grounding and navigation, but the Touchdown tasks are hard to reproduce without a vetted, versioned release. StreetLearn already has an approved, PII-checked, periodically updated distribution channel, so integrating Touchdown there makes it accessible and responsible.
key_idea: Release the 29,641 Touchdown Street View panoramas, manually reviewed and blurred for PII, as part of StreetLearn (Retouchdown), with reference VLN and SDR implementations that reproduce the original Touchdown results.
insight: Blurring PII regions does not hurt task performance. For SDR, running the model with features from the original panoramas gave similar results, so the differences from the original paper are not due to blurring. Retouchdown's absolute VLN numbers (TC 12.8, SDTW 1.4) are far below R2R, showing that outdoor Touchdown navigation leaves large headroom.
method: Panorama release: add the 29,641 Touchdown panoramas to StreetLearn (114k to 144k) via the existing form-based access process, with periodic updates for takedown compliance.
PII blurring: annotators manually review all panoramas and mark faces and license plates as bounding boxes, which are then blurred.
Retouch-LingUNet (SDR): re-implementation of the LingUNet spatial description resolution model on the blurred panoramas, using a word-piece tokenizer.
Retouch-RConcat (VLN): re-implementation of the RConcat navigation agent, trained with imitation learning on the VALAN Actor-Learner framework instead of Hogwild! supervised learning.
Open-source code: both tasks released in the VALAN framework, and nDTW and SDTW baselines are established for Touchdown.

setting.backbone: RConcat (VLN) and LingUNet (SDR), trained from scratch with a word-piece tokenizer
setting.training_data: Touchdown training data (9,326 navigation instructions, 27,575 SDR tasks) on blurred StreetLearn panoramas
setting.observation: Street View panoramas (image features) plus natural language instruction
setting.action_space: discrete Street View panorama graph navigation (forward/turn)
setting.simulator: StreetLearn / Street View panorama graph (New York City)

numbers.extra: Imitation learning on VALAN; blurred panoramas from StreetLearn

numbers_note: Touchdown is not in the canonical benchmark list, so 'Touchdown' is used as the name for the navigation rows (the canonical list has 'Touchdown' as an entry). Development results are labeled 'val'.
results: Retouch-RConcat improves on the original Touchdown paper's navigation results, with test TC 12.8 versus 10.7 and SPD 17.1 versus 19.5. Retouch-LingUNet improves SDR accuracy, with A@40px 30.32 versus 26.11, but its mean distance error is worse (793 versus 708). The blurred panoramas therefore fully support both tasks.
limitations: Absolute VLN performance is very low, and differences from the original paper come from implementation changes (imitation learning, word-piece tokenizer), so the comparison is not perfectly controlled.
The dataset is limited to Manhattan and requires a request form and periodic updates.
Only one model per task is reproduced, and the blurring check was done for SDR only.
